title_ar: قال فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو مهنئا الشيخ محمد سيديا (النووي) ولد سليمان ولد اجدود ترحيبا بابنه الغالي عبد الله، حفظهما الله تعالى
title_en: His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew Congratulates Sheikh Muhammad Sidiya (al-Nawawi) Ould Sulayman Ould Ajdud on the Welcome of His Beloved Son Abdullah — May God Almighty Preserve Them Both
body_ar:
قال فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو مهنئا الشيخ محمد سيديا (النووي) ولد سليمان ولد اجدود ترحيبا بابنه الغالي عبد الله، حفظهما الله تعالى

أعبد الله عش قرنا حميدا

كريما مكرما برا سعيدا

و كن كأبيك عالم كل فن

و للسنن المماتة مستعيدا

و للنهج القويم الزمْ و صنه

فعن وسط المحجة لن تحيدا

و للقرآن رتّل ذاك دأب

للابا كان دأبهم التليدا

حباك الله مما قد حباهم

و زادك رفعة و هدى مزيدا

و كن للشيخ ظلا و احو ما قد

حوى للطالبين فكن مفيدا

و سارع للمكارم و المعالي

و عش في ظله عيشا رغيدا

لنصر الحق فاسع و كن شجاعا

كأهليك الكرام و مت شهيدا
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew said, congratulating Sheikh Muhammad Sidiya (al-Nawawi) Ould Sulayman Ould Ajdud in welcome of his beloved son Abdullah — may God Almighty preserve them both:

O Abdullah, live out an age that is praiseworthy,

noble, honoured, dutiful and happy.

Be like your father, a scholar of every discipline,

and one who restores the sunnah practices that have fallen into disuse.

Hold fast to the upright way and guard it,

and you will never swerve from the middle of the road.

Recite the Qur'an measuredly; that was their constant practice,

the practice of the forefathers, their long-inherited way.

May God give you of what He gave them,

and increase you in elevation and in further guidance.

Be a shade for the sheikh, and gather what he has

gathered for the students, and so be of benefit.

Hasten to acts of nobility and to high things,

and live in his shade a life of ease.

Strive for the victory of the truth, and be brave

like your noble family, and die a martyr.

flags.context: و للقرآن رتّل ذاك دأب / للابا كان دأبهم التليدا
options: of the forefathers, their long-inherited way
of the fathers, whose inherited custom it was
read as للآباء, elided for the metre
flags.note: للابا is not a standard orthographic form. It reads most naturally as للآباء ('of the fathers') shortened for the metre, a common licence in Mauritanian nazm, but it could also be a CMS typo. Left as served in body_ar and not restored, per style guide section 11.

flags.context: و كن للشيخ ظلا و احو ما قد حوى للطالبين فكن مفيدا
options: Be a shade for the sheikh
Be a shelter to the sheikh
flags.note: ظل in this idiom is protection and support, not literal shade. 'الشيخ' here is the addressee's father, the dedicatee of the poem, rather than Sheikh al-Dedew himself; the referent is not explicit in the Arabic and should be confirmed.

flags.context: لنصر الحق فاسع و كن شجاعا كأهليك الكرام و مت شهيدا
options: and die as one who bears witness
and may your end be that of a martyr
flags.note: EDITORIAL NOTE. 'Die a martyr' is the literal and conventional rendering of the classical formula and is a standard closing benediction in Arabic congratulatory verse, not an incitement. Read in English out of context it can be misread. Translated faithfully, neither softened nor strengthened; the display context should make the genre clear.

flags.note: OVERLAPPING RECORDS. Record 1257, posted eight minutes later, reproduces this record's introduction and all sixteen lines of the poem verbatim and then adds Sheikh Abdullah Ajdud's reply. This is not the same defect as an identical duplicate: 1257 is a superset. Flagged; style guide section 11 reserves the deduplication decision to the Sheikh's office.

translator_notes: Verse (nazm). Style guide section 4 requires verse to be rendered as prose in italics with the Arabic retained in the bilingual pane; body_ar carries the Arabic line for line and body_en keeps the same line division so the two panes align. No rhymed English has been attempted.

Genre: poetry, filed by the site under الشعر (Poetry). The schema's type list has no value for poetry, so 'article' has been used; the genre is recorded here and in section/category. The schema should gain a poetry type.

The CMS uses the whole opening sentence as the record's title and then repeats it as the first line of the body. Both are kept: title_ar/title_en as the heading, and the sentence again at the head of the body, because it is the poem's prose introduction and not CMS furniture.
Mauritanian names are given in the local form: 'Ould' for ولد ('son of'), and 'Ajdud' for اجدود. Proper names carry no diacritics in body text, per style guide section 2.
No ruling of any kind is given, so the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3 is not engaged.

The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload/publication stamp, not the date on which the Sheikh gave the answer. Records across this range carry timestamps clustered minutes apart on the same day (e.g. 1275-1278 at 09:51/09:53/09:54/09:55 on 7 March 2022), which is the signature of a batch upload. date_is_cms_upload is therefore set true throughout.
